s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neck pain with stiffness and fever
salient_findings: Firm swelling in the posterior triangle of the left neck
key_facts: No dysphagia, dyspnea, or visual disturbances
CT and MRI showing poorly defined collection and intramuscular abscess in the left levator scapulae muscle

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute neck pain with stiffness and fever
salient_findings: Firm swelling in the posterior triangle of the left neck
key_facts: No dysphagia, dyspnea, or visual disturbances
CT and MRI showing poorly defined collection and intramuscular abscess in the left levator scapulae muscle

shortlist.label: Fusobacterium necrophorum infection
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by microbiological culture and consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Lemierre's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Associated with Fusobacterium necrophorum infection and can cause neck pain and stiffness

shortlist.label: Paraspinal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies show intramuscular abscess in the left levator scapulae muscle, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cervical spine infection
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and imaging studies suggest infection in the cervical spine region

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Although not confirmed, Staphylococcus is a common cause of abscesses and cannot be ruled out without further testing

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of neck pain, stiffness, and swelling, combined with imaging studies showing a poorly defined collection and intramuscular abscess in the left levator scapulae muscle, strongly supports the diagnosis of a paraspinal abscess.

rejected.label: Fusobacterium necrophorum infection
rejected.why: While F necrophorum infection is present, it is more likely a cause of the abscess rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lemierre's syndrome
rejected.why: Lemierre's syndrome typically involves septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Cervical spine infection
rejected.why: There is no evidence of osteomyelitis or discitis on the MRI, making cervical spine infection less likely.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal abscess
rejected.why: The microbiological culture identified F necrophorum, not Staphylococcus, as the causative organism.
